title: Using the Hundred Chart to Add

steps.body: On a hundred chart, 34 sits directly above 44. Moving down one row adds ten.
steps.narration: On a hundred chart, 34 sits directly above 44. Moving down one row adds ten.

widget.prompt: On the hundred chart, 27 is one row up from your target. Hop down one row (add ten).
widget.missFeedback: Start at 27 and count on 10: you land on 37.
widget.successFeedback: Landed on 37 — moving down one row on the chart adds ten.

predict.prompt: On a hundred chart, which direction adds ten?
predict.reveal: Each row of a hundred chart is a new ten, so moving down one row adds exactly ten.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g1a chart add.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for g1a chart add must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines g1a chart add.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: The hundred chart makes the tens-only change visible as a move down a row.
This matches exactly what happens when you add ten mentally.

commonErrors.feedback: That adds 1 one instead of 1 ten.
That forgets to add the tens.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Represent the two numbers, apply the shown operation, and check the result.

hints: Down one row on the chart means add ten.
